title: Reliable background sync
summary: Exercise retries, cancellation, outbox delivery, and diagnostics under unreliable networks.
outcome: A tested sync pipeline that survives ambiguous responses and explains its current state to users.
prerequisites: Finish service Layers and shared projects. Read src/db/sync/engine.ts, outbox.ts, and ownership.ts before proposing changes.
model: Outbox operation: stable operationId, entityId, payload/revision, attempt count, nextAttemptAt, status.
Server receipt: unique (userId, operationId) paired transactionally with the business write.
Sync states: idle, queued, running, blocked, retrying; define which errors require user intervention.
boundaries: Local transaction + outbox → scoped worker → authenticated API → atomic receipt and write → conditional local acknowledgement.

milestones.title: Bound retries and timeouts
milestones.brief: Retry temporary network failures without retrying invalid input or expired authorization forever.
milestones.explanation: Retry policy follows failure meaning. A 503 may be temporary; validation and permission failures usually require a change. A timeout means the response was not observed, not that the server did nothing. Bound attempts and elapsed time, and respect server retry guidance where applicable.
steps: Write an error table: network/429/503, validation, denied access, conflict, and unexpected defect. Specify retry or user action for each.
Use a capped retry schedule with backoff, jitter, a per-attempt timeout, and a total budget. Keep timing controllable in tests.
Use public/workshop/fixtures/fake-service.mjs or an injected fake transport to exercise 429, 503, then success. Expose a retry state and last useful error.

checks.label: Transient failures retry within a finite attempt and elapsed-time budget.
Validation, permission, and conflict failures do not enter a blind retry loop.
Timing tests run deterministically without real long sleeps.

milestones.experiment: Have the transport fail on every attempt. Measure attempts and final state; verify the operation eventually stops retrying.
milestones.review: Distinguish defects from expected operational failures. Log enough context to diagnose the attempt without logging tokens or private payloads.
milestones.stretch: Add a shared rate limit so multiple queued items do not each retry at the maximum rate.

milestones.title: Deliver writes without duplicates
milestones.brief: Survive a successful server write whose response is lost before the client receives it.
milestones.explanation: A retryable write needs a durable identity. Persist the local change and its outbox record together. On the server, record the operation receipt and business write atomically. Acknowledge only the exact outbox version that was sent so a newer local edit is not accidentally removed.
steps: Define a stable operation ID, payload policy, and server duplicate response. Reject reuse of the same ID with a different payload.
Simulate delivery, server commit, lost response, and client retry. Keep the receipt and mutation inside the same server transaction.
Test a newer local edit arriving while the older request is in flight. Remove the old outbox entry only if it still matches the sent version.

checks.label: A committed write with a lost response is applied only once after retry.
A local write cannot commit without its required outbox entry.
Acknowledging an older request never deletes a newer queued edit.

milestones.experiment: Commit the server mutation, drop its response, then restart the client. Check both the final entity and operation-receipt counts.
milestones.review: A client-side disabled button cannot provide server idempotency. Explain receipt retention and what happens after the retention window.
milestones.stretch: Add a dead-letter view for operations that require manual resolution.

milestones.title: Own worker lifetime and diagnostics
milestones.brief: Stop stale work on logout and make sync behavior understandable after reconnects.
milestones.explanation: Background work needs an owner and a lifetime. Scope workers and resources so cleanup happens on shutdown. Interruption stops local work cooperatively; it cannot reverse a remote commit. Guard identity and request generation before applying a late result.
steps: Define startup, reconnect, account logout, and application shutdown behavior. Ensure repeated setup does not register duplicate workers or listeners.
Cancel or interrupt the active worker when its owner changes, pass cancellation to transports that support it, and reject stale responses.
Add operation IDs, attempt numbers, duration, and categorized failures to diagnostics. Expose pending and blocked counts with an explicit retry action.

checks.label: Repeated startup or reconnect produces only one active worker per scope.
Logout prevents late results from updating a different account's state.
A recorded operation ID traces queueing, attempts, and final acknowledgement.

milestones.experiment: Pause a request, log out, then release its response. Verify no stale UI update or cross-account local write occurs.
milestones.review: Explain which effects can be interrupted and which remote consequences may already be durable. Inspect listener and timer cleanup.
milestones.stretch: Measure queue drain time before and after adding bounded concurrency without breaking per-entity ordering.

milestones.title: Prevent stale cached responses
milestones.brief: Add a read cache whose keys, invalidation, and logout behavior preserve account boundaries and current edits.
milestones.explanation: A cache key must contain every input that changes the result, including identity and filters. Expiry limits staleness but does not itself invalidate an edited record. A late response may be valid for an older request while being wrong for the current screen. Treat cached data, pending mutations, and authoritative server state as separate concerns.
steps: Write cache keys for project detail and filtered lists. Specify expiration, successful-write invalidation, and account-switch cleanup.
Implement bounded storage and invalidate related queries after a committed mutation. Use a request generation or cancellation to prevent obsolete responses from replacing current results.
Test two identities requesting the same record ID, rapid filter changes, and a slow pre-edit read completing after an edit.

checks.label: Cache entries never leak between users or filter combinations.
A completed edit becomes visible without waiting for arbitrary expiry.
Late responses cannot replace results for a newer request.

milestones.experiment: Start a slow read, save a new title, then resolve the old read. Inspect the final title and identify the guard that prevents regression.
milestones.review: Explain when stale data is acceptable and how the interface signals it. A cache that makes a permission change invisible indefinitely is a correctness problem.
milestones.stretch: Measure hit rate and request count, then justify whether caching this particular query is worth its invalidation complexity.

milestones.title: Drain an outbox with bounded concurrency
milestones.brief: Improve queue throughput while keeping edits to the same entity ordered and respecting service limits.
milestones.explanation: Launching every queued request at once can overload the browser and server. A concurrency limit bounds simultaneous work, but does not automatically preserve ordering for operations on one record. Partition by an appropriate key or serialize dependencies, then allow independent entities to proceed together. Measure throughput without weakening delivery semantics.
steps: Create a fixture with repeated edits to one project and independent writes to several others. Define which operations may run concurrently.
Add a bounded worker pool or equivalent Effect concurrency setting. Preserve required per-entity order and ensure a failed item does not starve unrelated work.
Record maximum active requests, queue drain time, and final revisions under slow, failed, and rate-limited transports.

checks.label: Active requests never exceed the configured concurrency limit.
Same-entity operations preserve the declared ordering rule.
Independent records continue progressing when one item is blocked.

milestones.experiment: Delay an early edit while allowing a later edit to finish quickly. Verify the final server version is correct under your ordering or conditional-write policy.
milestones.review: Distinguish concurrency from rate: four active requests can still exceed a requests-per-second limit. Keep both policies observable and independently testable.
milestones.stretch: Introduce weighted fairness so a large import cannot indefinitely delay an interactive user edit.

milestones.title: Repair divergence after a long outage
milestones.brief: Reconnect a device that missed several edits and deletions, then reconcile without resurrecting removed records or discarding local work.
milestones.explanation: A reconnect is not always a simple replay. Deletion markers, cursor retention, and unresolved local edits determine whether incremental sync is still valid. If a server cursor is too old, define a full reconciliation path. Never treat absence from a single paginated response as proof that a record was deleted.
steps: Build a fixture with two devices, a remote deletion, a local unsent edit, and an expired incremental cursor. Write the intended conflict outcomes.
Implement the recovery path with complete pagination and explicit deletion information. Preserve unresolved drafts and explain conflicts to the user.
Interrupt reconciliation halfway, restart it, and compare final records and outbox entries. Verify repeated recovery is safe.

checks.label: Remote deletions do not silently resurrect after reconnect.
Local unsent work is retained or explicitly presented for resolution.
Interrupted reconciliation can restart without duplication or data loss.

milestones.experiment: Remove a record remotely after the first reconciliation page is fetched. Verify your snapshot or version policy handles changes during the scan.
milestones.review: State assumptions about server history retention and clock ordering. Record where manual resolution is necessary rather than hiding ambiguity behind last-write-wins.
milestones.stretch: Create a read-only diagnostic report comparing local and remote identities before any repair writes occur.

milestones.title: Retry only transient failures
milestones.brief: A sync request alternates between validation failure, connection reset, and permission denial.
milestones.explanation: Retries are justified by failure semantics rather than by any rejected promise.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: A sync request alternates between validation failure, connection reset, and permission denial. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Define typed permanent, transient, and ambiguous-result categories.
Inject each category and count attempts. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The transient failure follows the bounded retry policy.
Validation and permission failures stop without repeated requests.
Recovery evidence: Return a permanent error after two transient failures. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Return a permanent error after two transient failures.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does retry logic inspect domain variants instead of matching message text?
milestones.stretch: Add a table documenting retry decisions for every external error category.

milestones.title: Cap total retry duration
milestones.brief: A request has a five-second timeout and can retry four times with delays.
milestones.explanation: Attempt limits alone do not establish a useful overall latency bound.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: A request has a five-second timeout and can retry four times with delays. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Define both per-attempt timeout and total operation deadline.
Use a controlled clock to run repeated slow failures. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The operation stops within its documented total budget.
Backoff delays cannot extend work indefinitely past the deadline.
Recovery evidence: Begin the final attempt with less time than its usual timeout. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Begin the final attempt with less time than its usual timeout.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the implementation pass the remaining budget to the attempt?
milestones.stretch: Expose a user-visible retry action after automatic retries are exhausted.

milestones.title: Jitter synchronized clients
milestones.brief: One hundred clients reconnect after an outage and receive the same transient error.
milestones.explanation: Identical backoff schedules can synchronize load spikes across clients.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: One hundred clients reconnect after an outage and receive the same transient error. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Add bounded jitter through an injectable random source.
Compare scheduled times with a fixed deterministic random sequence. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Retry delays stay within the declared range and attempt budget.
Clients do not all retry at the exact same instant.
Recovery evidence: Set random values to their minimum and maximum extremes. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Set random values to their minimum and maximum extremes.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does jitter accidentally permit negative or excessive delays?
milestones.stretch: Simulate a reconnect wave and compare peak request rate before and after jitter.

milestones.title: Respect server retry guidance
milestones.brief: A service returns a retry-after hint longer than the client's usual backoff.
milestones.explanation: Server guidance needs parsing, caps, and compatibility with the total deadline.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: A service returns a retry-after hint longer than the client's usual backoff. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Interpret supported hint forms and clamp them to the documented policy.
Test valid, malformed, past, and excessive retry hints. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Accepted hints influence scheduling within the total budget.
Malformed headers never create NaN timers or immediate tight loops.
Recovery evidence: Return a hint beyond the remaining operation deadline. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Return a hint beyond the remaining operation deadline.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the user receive an understandable deferred or exhausted state?
milestones.stretch: Persist a next-eligible-at time when background work must survive restart.

milestones.title: Keep timeout outcomes honest
milestones.brief: A create request times out after the server has already committed the row.
milestones.explanation: Timeout proves lack of a timely response, not absence of a durable side effect.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: A create request times out after the server has already committed the row. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Use stable command identity and reconciliation for uncertain write outcomes.
Commit remotely, drop the response, then retry. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The server retains one row for the original command.
The client never blindly creates a new identity after timeout.
Recovery evidence: Reconnect after reloading the application. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Reconnect after reloading the application.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the operation distinguish retrying delivery from issuing a new user command?
milestones.stretch: Add a status endpoint keyed by command identity.

milestones.title: Stop retries on cancellation
milestones.brief: Cancel sync while the worker is waiting between attempts.
milestones.explanation: Cancellation should prevent future attempts and release owned timers.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Cancel sync while the worker is waiting between attempts. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Tie retry scheduling to the worker's interruption scope.
Cancel during request, delay, and final result handling. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: No new attempt starts after cancellation settles.
Timers and listeners do not survive the canceled worker.
Recovery evidence: Cancel at the exact boundary when the next attempt becomes eligible. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Cancel at the exact boundary when the next attempt becomes eligible.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Can a queued callback start work after scope disposal?
milestones.stretch: Add deterministic tests using a controlled clock rather than real sleeps.

milestones.title: Preserve the original cause
milestones.brief: Three connection failures exhaust the retry schedule with different low-level causes.
milestones.explanation: A final error should retain enough cause history to explain exhaustion safely.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Three connection failures exhaust the retry schedule with different low-level causes. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Record attempt count, categories, and sanitized final cause.
Inspect the final typed failure and user-facing message. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Diagnostics identify the retry budget and relevant cause.
The user message contains no raw credential-bearing request data.
Recovery evidence: Make the final failure differ from the first two. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Make the final failure differ from the first two.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does wrapping replace every useful cause with a generic timeout string?
milestones.stretch: Attach a correlation ID linking operation history across attempts.

milestones.title: Avoid nested retry multiplication
milestones.brief: The HTTP adapter retries three times and the sync operation also retries three times.
milestones.explanation: Layered retries can multiply attempts and exceed the intended latency budget.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: The HTTP adapter retries three times and the sync operation also retries three times. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Choose one retry owner or explicitly divide budgets across layers.
Count actual network calls under persistent transient failure. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Observed attempts match the documented overall limit.
Three-by-three hidden retry multiplication cannot occur.
Recovery evidence: Add a timeout wrapper around both layers and inspect cancellation. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Add a timeout wrapper around both layers and inspect cancellation.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does each abstraction document whether it retries internally?
milestones.stretch: Expose attempt metadata so higher layers can enforce an end-to-end budget.

milestones.title: Test retry schedules deterministically
milestones.brief: A flaky test waits real seconds for a backoff schedule to complete.
milestones.explanation: Time-dependent behavior should be verified through controllable time and dependencies.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: A flaky test waits real seconds for a backoff schedule to complete. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Inject or provide the test clock and deterministic failure sequence.
Advance through each scheduled boundary and count requests. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: No request starts before its scheduled eligibility.
The final result appears at the expected controlled time.
Recovery evidence: Advance past several deadlines in one jump. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Advance past several deadlines in one jump.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the test assert schedule semantics rather than implementation timer calls?
milestones.stretch: Add property checks for monotonic bounded next-attempt times.

milestones.title: Commit intent with local mutation
milestones.brief: Edit a project locally while network delivery is unavailable.
milestones.explanation: The local change and its delivery intent must become durable together.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Edit a project locally while network delivery is unavailable. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Write the project update and outbox entry in one transaction.
Fail each write position independently and inspect both tables. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Successful local edits have exactly one corresponding delivery intent.
No unsent local mutation exists without an outbox record.
Recovery evidence: Crash immediately after the transaction commits. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Crash immediately after the transaction commits.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the worker discover committed intent without relying on an in-memory event?
milestones.stretch: Add a startup drain that scans durable pending entries.

milestones.title: Deduplicate remote delivery
milestones.brief: Deliver one outbox command twice after losing the first successful response.
milestones.explanation: At-least-once delivery requires an idempotent receiver for one logical command.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Deliver one outbox command twice after losing the first successful response. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Send a stable operation ID and persist the server's receipt atomically with mutation.
Replay the command with the same identity. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Remote state changes once and returns a consistent receipt.
Duplicate delivery cannot increment revision or counters twice.
Recovery evidence: Reuse the identity with different payload content. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Reuse the identity with different payload content.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the receiver reject inconsistent reuse rather than accepting changed intent?
milestones.stretch: Store a payload digest with the idempotency receipt.

milestones.title: Delete only acknowledged entries
milestones.brief: The server accepts a command but the client crashes before processing its acknowledgment.
milestones.explanation: An outbox entry remains pending until acknowledgment is durably recorded.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: The server accepts a command but the client crashes before processing its acknowledgment. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Apply the receipt and remove or mark the entry in one local transaction.
Crash before and after the local acknowledgment transaction. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Restart safely redelivers or recognizes the acknowledged command.
Pending intent is never deleted merely because a request was sent.
Recovery evidence: Return a malformed acknowledgment after remote success. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Return a malformed acknowledgment after remote success.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does receipt validation happen before local queue cleanup?
milestones.stretch: Keep a bounded archive of acknowledged receipts for diagnostics.

milestones.title: Preserve per-entity order
milestones.brief: Queue create, rename, and archive for the same project while offline.
milestones.explanation: Dependent commands must reach the receiver in an order compatible with their assumptions.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Queue create, rename, and archive for the same project while offline. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Track entity sequence or dependencies and block later commands until predecessors settle.
Make rename's network response faster than create's response. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The server observes the intended project lifecycle.
Archive cannot overtake an uncommitted create for the same entity.
Recovery evidence: Fail the first command permanently. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Fail the first command permanently.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the queue mark dependent commands blocked instead of retrying them blindly?
milestones.stretch: Allow unrelated entities to progress concurrently despite one blocked chain.

milestones.title: Handle poison entries visibly
milestones.brief: One outbox command has an invalid field and fails every delivery attempt.
milestones.explanation: Permanent failure must leave a visible repairable record without blocking unrelated work forever.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: One outbox command has an invalid field and fails every delivery attempt. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Classify the entry as failed with safe reason and explicit repair actions.
Queue valid commands before and after the invalid entry. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Valid independent commands still synchronize.
The poison entry never disappears or retries in a tight loop.
Recovery evidence: Edit the underlying entity after the entry becomes failed. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Edit the underlying entity after the entry becomes failed.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does repair create new intent rather than mutating historical command identity?
milestones.stretch: Add exportable diagnostics and an explicit abandon action with consequences explained.

milestones.title: Coalesce only compatible edits
milestones.brief: Offline edits change a project's goal three times before any delivery begins.
milestones.explanation: Coalescing is safe only when intermediate commands carry no required independent semantics.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Offline edits change a project's goal three times before any delivery begins. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Define eligible patch coalescing and preserve the earliest base revision.
Compare final state with sequential execution of the original commands. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The coalesced command produces the same allowed final domain state.
Create, archive, audit, or dependent operations are not collapsed indiscriminately.
Recovery evidence: Insert a command from another workflow between the edits. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Insert a command from another workflow between the edits.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does optimization preserve causality and idempotency receipts?
milestones.stretch: Measure queue reduction while retaining an explanation of coalesced user actions.

milestones.title: Survive browser restart
milestones.brief: Create three offline changes, close the browser, and reopen with connectivity restored.
milestones.explanation: Queue durability must not depend on component memory or an open tab.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Create three offline changes, close the browser, and reopen with connectivity restored. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Load pending entries from storage during worker startup.
Restart using the same persisted fixture and inspect delivered identities. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: All three commands remain available and deliver once logically.
No command is regenerated with a new identity on startup.
Recovery evidence: Crash after delivering the first command but before local acknowledgment. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Crash after delivering the first command but before local acknowledgment.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does startup reconcile in-flight entries left by the prior process?
milestones.stretch: Add durable attempt metadata without treating old in-flight flags as permanent locks.

milestones.title: Keep payload versions explicit
milestones.brief: An older queued command remains on disk when a new app version changes the update schema.
milestones.explanation: Outbox payloads are durable contracts that may outlive the code that created them.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: An older queued command remains on disk when a new app version changes the update schema. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Store a payload version and route old commands through supported adapters.
Upgrade with pending old-version entries and drain them. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Supported old commands retain their original meaning.
Unknown command versions are quarantined instead of guessed.
Recovery evidence: Introduce a renamed field in the new command decoder. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Introduce a renamed field in the new command decoder.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the migration preserve operation IDs while adapting payload shape?
milestones.stretch: Add historical outbox fixtures to release compatibility checks.

milestones.title: Separate discard from undo
milestones.brief: A user discards a queued archive command after it may have reached the server.
milestones.explanation: Removing local intent cannot guarantee reversal of an already accepted remote mutation.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: A user discards a queued archive command after it may have reached the server. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Define pending, in-flight, acknowledged, and uncertain discard behavior.
Attempt discard in each delivery state. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The UI accurately explains whether cancellation is still possible.
Discard never claims the server action was undone without evidence.
Recovery evidence: Lose the response during an in-flight discard attempt. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Lose the response during an in-flight discard attempt.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does undo issue a new compensating command with fresh preconditions?
milestones.stretch: Offer reconciliation before permitting a compensation based on uncertain remote state.

milestones.title: Own one worker per scope

milestones.explanation: A worker needs a clear owner so navigation does not duplicate background loops.

milestones.brief: The user pauses sync while the network is offline and a retry is scheduled.
